title: 2 Chronicles 29
paragraphs: ¹ Hezekiah became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah. ² He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father David had done. ³ In the first month of the first year of his reign, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them. ⁴ He brought in the priests and the Levites, assembled them in the square to the east, ⁵ and said: "Listen to me, Levites! Now consecrate yourselves and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your ancestors. Remove everything defiling from the sanctuary."

⁶ "For our ancestors were unfaithful; they did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD our God and forsook him. They turned away from the LORD's dwelling place and turned their backs on him. ⁷ They also shut the doors of the portico and put out the lamps. They have not burned incense or presented burnt offerings at the sanctuary of the God of Israel. ⁸ Therefore the anger of the LORD has fallen on Judah and Jerusalem; he has made them an object of dread and horror and scorn, as you can see with your own eyes. ⁹ This is why our fathers have fallen by the sword and why our sons, daughters, and wives are in captivity. ¹⁰ Now I intend to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that his fierce anger will turn away from us."

¹¹ "My sons, do not be negligent now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before him and serve him, to minister before him and to burn incense." ¹² Then the Levites rose: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah, from the Kohathites; Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel, from the Merarites; Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah, from the Gershonites; ¹³ Shimri and Jeiel, from the family of Elizaphan; Zechariah and Mattaniah, from the family of Asaph; ¹⁴ Jehiel and Shimei, from the family of Heman; and Shemaiah and Uzziel, from the family of Jeduthun. ¹⁵ They gathered their fellow Levites and consecrated themselves, then came in to purify the house of the LORD, as the king had commanded, following the word of the LORD.

¹⁶ The priests went into the inner chambers of the LORD's temple to purify it, carrying out everything unclean they found and bringing it to the courtyard of the LORD's house, where the Levites took it and hauled it out to the Kidron Valley. ¹⁷ They began the purification on the first day of the first month, and by the eighth day they had reached the LORD's porch; over the next eight days they sanctified the house of the LORD, and by the sixteenth day of the first month the work was finished. ¹⁸ Then they came in to King Hezekiah and reported, "We have cleansed the entire house of the LORD—the altar of burnt offering with all its equipment, and the table of the showbread with all its vessels. ¹⁹ Every piece that King Ahaz threw aside during his reign of unfaithfulness, we have prepared and consecrated. They are now standing before the altar of the LORD." ²⁰ Hezekiah rose early the next morning, gathered the leaders of the city, and went up to the house of the LORD.

²¹ They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. The king commanded the priests, the sons of Aaron, to offer them on the altar of the LORD. ²² So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests caught the blood and splashed it against the altar; they slaughtered the rams and splashed their blood on the altar; they slaughtered the lambs and splashed their blood on the altar as well. ²³ Then the male goats were brought before the king and the assembly for the sin offering, and they laid their hands on them. ²⁴ The priests slaughtered them and made atonement with their blood on the altar for all Israel, because the king had commanded that the burnt offering and sin offering be made on behalf of all Israel. ²⁵ He stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres, according to the command of David, the prophet Gad the king's seer, and the prophet Nathan — for this was the LORD's command through his prophets.

²⁶ The Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with their trumpets. ²⁷ Then Hezekiah gave the order for the burnt offering to be placed on the altar. The moment the offering began, the song of the LORD broke out, accompanied by the trumpets and the instruments that David king of Israel had prescribed. ²⁸ The whole assembly worshipped as the singers sang and the trumpeters sounded — and this continued until the burnt offering was complete. ²⁹ When the offering was finished, the king and everyone with him bowed down and worshipped. ³⁰ Hezekiah the king and his officials commanded the Levites to sing praises to the LORD in the words of David and Asaph the seer. They sang with great joy, and they bowed their heads and worshipped.

³¹ Then Hezekiah spoke up: "Now that you have dedicated yourselves to the LORD, come forward and bring your sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD." The assembly brought in sacrifices and thank offerings, and all whose hearts moved them freely brought burnt offerings as well. ³² The total of burnt offerings brought by the congregation came to seventy bulls, a hundred rams, and two hundred lambs — all for the LORD. ³³ The consecrated gifts amounted to six hundred oxen and three thousand sheep. ³⁴ But there were not enough priests to skin all the burnt offerings, so their fellow Levites helped them until the work was done and until the other priests had consecrated themselves — the Levites had been more conscientious about consecrating themselves than the priests had been. ³⁵ In addition to all this, there were abundant burnt offerings along with the fat of the fellowship offerings and the drink offerings for every burnt offering. So the service of the house of the LORD was fully restored.
³⁶ Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced, for God had prepared everything so quickly — the whole thing had happened in a matter of days.
